# Executing Your Service Menu — Concrete Steps for Grace

• **Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now** — Have your coaches list every service/variation they've sold in the last 3 months (group classes, 1-on-1s, nutrition plans, challenges, memberships tiers, etc.). You'll find gaps and duplicates. This is your raw material.

• **Price backwards from member willingness-to-pay, not your costs** — Interview 5-10 members separately. Ask: "What would make you upgrade?" and "At what price would you feel ripped off?" Your coaches won't know this. Use those numbers to anchor your tiers, not what you *think* is fair.

• **Create TWO menus: a simple one-pager for members, a detailed operations manual for coaches** — Members see pricing + what's included in plain language (e.g., "Unlimited group classes + 1 monthly form check"). Coaches get: exact service definitions, what you upsell after, common objections + answers, and commissions if they're incentivized. Coaches need to sell the same thing consistently.

• **Lock in your offer NOW, even if imperfect** — Don't wait for the "perfect" menu. Test one version for 4 weeks, track what converts and what confuses people, then refine. You'll learn more from real pushback than planning.

• **Assign ONE person (probably you) as the gatekeeper** — Every time a coach wants to offer something custom or discount, they check with you first. This prevents menu creep and keeps your positioning clear.

What's your current pricing structure like? That'll tell me what's most urgent to clarify first.
